summary: Unexpected redistribution of daily metering across projects causing overcharge on consolidated invoice
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports a sudden reallocation of usage (daily metering) across three internal projects on their consolidated invoice for 2026-03-08. Usage that historically billed to project-prod-usa has appeared as billed to project-data-poc and project-internal-tests, triggering an unexpected overage on the consolidated invoice and breaking cost-center accounting.

Observed behavior / Timeline:
- 2026-03-08 00:00 - 08:00 UTC: multiple large batch embedding jobs run from BrightCart's orchestration cluster.
- 2026-03-08 09:12 UTC: customer notices unexplained spike on Console usage page; support ticket opened.
- 2026-03-08 10:00 UTC: customer exported per-project usage CSV and found token counts redistributed between project IDs.
- 2026-03-08 14:30 UTC: engineering initial triage observed reorder of postbacks during a reconciliation job backfill executed 2026-03-08 01:40 UTC.

Impact:
- Overcharge of approximately $5,900 on consolidated invoice for billing day 2026-03-08.
- Internal chargeback mismatches for three Cost Centers at BrightCart (finance needs retroactive correction).
- Customer unable to reconcile budgets; requested provisional credit and root cause explanation for auditors.

Environment:
prod | us-east-1
Redwood components involved: metering-postback-reconciler, hourly-aggregator, billing-tag-mapper
Affected models: text-embed-512, text-qa-2b (in mixed-job batches)

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule a mixed-model batch embed job from BrightCart orchestration using api key tied to project-prod-usa at 2026-03-08 00:10 UTC.
2) Trigger a metadata tag migration on the org that renames some api-key tags to new project prefixes during the same billing window.
3) Run a manual reconciler backfill job for legacy postbacks (the backfill was run 2026-03-08 01:40 UTC in this incident).
4) Observe hourly-aggregator outputs and consolidated invoice; token counts appear split across projects rather than attributed to original project-prod-usa.
5) Export Console per-project usage for 2026-03-08 and compare CSVs before and after backfill; differences reproduce the redistribution in our environment replica.
investigation_notes:
Initial findings:
- Postback ordering during the backfill appears to have re-applied a tag remapping table that was mid-migration. The billing-tag-mapper accepted both old and new prefixes during reconciliation, leading to split attribution for identical usage fingerprints.
- Logs from metering-postback-reconciler show duplicate acknowledgements for a subset of postbacks (IDs in logs around 2026-03-08T01:42Z).
- Hourly-aggregator committed intermediate windows with mixed project tags before the backfill completed, creating persistent downstream ledger entries.
- No invoice-line level rounding or currency conversion faults observed; root cause looks like tag reclassification race during backfill.

Hypothesis: a backfill + tag-migration race caused deterministic but inconsistent mapping for postbacks emitted in the same hourly window. The reconciler's idempotency key logic allowed re-attribution when encountering postbacks with updated tags instead of merging to the original attribution.

Preliminary mitigation applied 2026-03-10 15:20 UTC: disabled the legacy-backfill job queue for org-level tag operations and forced a consistency pass to re-merge hourly windows for 2026-03-08. Re-merge job shows candidate correction but requires finance approval before issuing provisional credits.
customer_request: BrightCart requests: 1) provisional credit equal to the overcharged amount ($5,900) applied to their account while we complete re-merge; 2) a clear root-cause writeup for auditors including timeline and steps we will take to prevent recurrence; 3) confirmation of any action required on their side (no changes planned).
workarounds_and_next_steps:
Workarounds:
- Customer should not run tag-migration backfills during hourly-billing windows until reconciler fix deploy.
- For immediate relief we've offered a provisional credit pending final re-merge and finance approval.

Next steps (owned by teams):
- Billing team to approve provisional credit (Finance ticket required).
- Metering team to deploy a reconciler patch that enforces idempotent attribution by locking original attribution key during backfills (PR referenced above).
- SRE to run full re-merge for 2026-03-08 and validate ledger parity with pre-backfill snapshots.
- Postmortem and runbook update to prevent backfill/tag-change concurrency in billing windows.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Jamie Chen (Billing): Confirmed invoice line shows unexpected lines for project-data-poc and project-internal-tests; estimating impact ~$5.9k. Opening finance approval request. Linked INT-3152 for internal reconciliation.

2026-03-10 14:50 - Priya Malhotra (Metering Eng): Found backfill job executed 2026-03-08 01:40 UTC; reconciler log indicates ambiguous tag mapping for ~1,240 postbacks. Hypothesis: tag migration table was updated mid-run. Preparing hotfix.
2026-03-10 16:05 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Disabled legacy-backfill queue for affected orgs and kicked off consistency re-merge. Re-merge running; will report parity results in next comment.
2026-03-11 10:30 - Jamie Chen (Billing): Finance approved provisional credit for BrightCart pending final re-merge validation. Issued temporary credit hold and notified customer operations.
2026-03-12 09:25 - Thomas Vega (Customer): Thanks, we saw the provisional credit reflected in Console. Please confirm when final adjustment posts and share RCA for auditors.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11 provisional credit of $5,900 applied to BrightCart account as a temporary hold. Final ledger adjustment to post after SRE re-merge validates parity. Metering team PR merged to enforce attribution idempotency; runbook updated to block backfills during billing windows. Finance will publish final credit and adjusted invoice upon completion.
